label: Moved by something, by another, per accidens
term: moved by something (ὑπό τινος), by another, per accidens
resolution: Three different claims about a moved thing's mover. 'By something' (ὑπό τινος) allows the thing itself; 'by another' (ὑπʼ ἄλλου, `MovedByAnother`) requires a distinct mover; a per accidens mover (`MovesPerAccidensIn`) is a mover only in a way. `MovesIn` is always per se moving, in the sense of DEF-MOTION-AS-REDUCTION. The literal reading of Physics VIII.4 (STMT-EVERY-MOVED-THING-MOVED-PER-SE-OR-PER-ACCIDENS) keeps the per accidens disjunct; a per se mover for physical motion follows only with the added, unattributed premise STMT-PER-ACCIDENS-MOVED-PASSIVE-MOTION-HAS-PER-SE-MOVER, and result ARIST-PHYS-VIII-4-EVERY-MOVED-PER-SE-OR-PER-ACCIDENS shows the literal reading does not yield STMT-EVERY-PHYSICAL-MOTION-HAS-A-PER-SE-MOVER. STMT-EVERY-MOVED-THING-HAS-SOME-MOVER is respect-free 'by something'; it is not the prima via's respect-indexed premise and is not identified with it. The same words ὑπό τινος are read differently at different places, and each record says which: at VIII.4, 256a2-3 (literal) per se or per accidens, in the same respect; in the forced and self-motion branches per se, in the same respect; at VII.1, 241b24 and VIII.5, 256a13-14 (STMT-EVERY-MOVED-THING-HAS-SOME-MOVER) per se, in some respect. The last is a stronger reading than VIII.4's literal conclusion and is not derived from it.
